items.title: Enforce that entry points cannot escape in the scripts directory
items.reason: This historical change retained the site-packages-relative launcher write but changed the Unix permission lookup to the intended scripts path. With the reported lib symlink, those paths resolve to different files.

related.search_scope: Searched exact error fragments, console_scripts and entry-point installation, site-packages/RECORD-relative paths, usr/bin, virtual-environment symlinks, script.as_path, and the cited commit across open and closed issues and all pull request states. No existing tracker covers this Unix failure. astral-sh/uv#18728, astral-sh/uv#19374, and astral-sh/uv#11048 were inspected but concern package listing, Windows launcher execution, and shebang selection, respectively.

type_reason: The installer writes the launcher through a site-packages-relative path and then queries permissions through the intended scripts path. A lib symlink can make those paths resolve differently, causing incorrect placement and installation failure. astral-sh/uv#19464 is historical context, not a duplicate tracker.
summary: No canonical duplicate was found. Merged security hardening astral-sh/uv#19464 is the closest related change and exposes the path mismatch under this symlinked layout.
draft_response:
Thanks for the focused reproduction. This is a bug, and the current installer code matches the behavior you found: the launcher is written using a path relative to site-packages, while the executable-permission step introduced in astral-sh/uv#19464 queries the intended scripts path directly. With `lib` resolving through `usr/lib`, those paths can refer to different locations, so the launcher lands under `usr/bin` and the subsequent lookup under `bin` fails.

The reproduction is sufficient. The next step is to add a Unix integration regression test for this virtual-environment layout and ensure the launcher write and permission update target the same scripts path while preserving the correct `RECORD` entry.
